scenes.tts: When you turn your head, your inner ear reports the turn. Does your brain treat it like a turn someone gave you?
scenes.visual: Title card: Only When the Feedback Matches. A monkey head turning, an inner-ear canal glowing. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: When you turn your head, your inner ear reports the turn. Does your brain treat it like a turn someone gave you?

scenes.tts: Start with the receptors. In alert monkeys, canal afferents report active and passive turns alike.
scenes.visual: A meter for canal afferents, labelled strength of motion-related modulation. Active turn: high. Passive turn: high. Caption: Cullen and Minor, 2002. Text: not in the ear.
scenes.narration: Start with the receptors. In alert monkeys, canal afferents report active and passive turns alike.

scenes.tts: In freely moving mice, Pacinian touch afferents also fire strongly to the animal's own movements.
scenes.visual: A freely moving mouse with an afferent spike trace firing in bursts during its own steps. Caption: Turecek and Ginty, 2024.
scenes.narration: In freely moving mice, Pacinian touch afferents also fire strongly to the animal's own movements.

scenes.tts: So the receptors pass self-caused input to the brain. Whether it is damped further along, that mouse study did not test.
scenes.visual: The mouse trace runs into a brain icon. Label: peripheral reafference recorded; downstream attenuation unmeasured.
scenes.narration: So the receptors pass self-caused input to the brain. Whether it is damped further along, that mouse study did not test.

scenes.tts: Back to the monkey. Central vestibular-only neurons respond to head motion, not to eye movement.
scenes.visual: A second meter appears, labelled vestibular-only neurons (central), strength of motion-related modulation. A steady background spike train runs beneath it.
scenes.narration: Back to the monkey. Central vestibular-only neurons respond to head motion, not to eye movement.

scenes.tts: An active turn barely changes their firing. The same turn applied passively changes it strongly.
scenes.visual: Row 1, active turn: afferent meter high, central meter low. Row 2, passive turn: both high. The background spike train continues at a similar baseline in both rows; only the turn-related swing differs.
scenes.narration: An active turn barely changes their firing. The same turn applied passively changes it strongly.

scenes.tts: Neck proprioceptors report how the head moves on the body. The cancellation needed them to match the command's prediction.
scenes.visual: Neck muscle sensors light up; a check mark where the feedback matches the predicted feedback. Caption: Roy and Cullen, 2004.
scenes.narration: Neck proprioceptors report how the head moves on the body. The cancellation needed them to match the command's prediction.

scenes.tts: Brooks and Cullen then added passive motion during an active turn, activating the same proprioceptors.
scenes.visual: Row 3 appears: active turn plus added passive motion. Caption: Brooks and Cullen, 2014.
scenes.narration: Brooks and Cullen then added passive motion during an active turn, activating the same proprioceptors.

scenes.tts: Predict. With the feedback no longer matching, what do the central neurons report?
scenes.visual: Row 3: afferent meter drawn dashed, labelled expected, not recorded; central meter shows a question mark. Text: Predict.
scenes.narration: Predict. With the feedback no longer matching, what do the central neurons report?

scenes.tts: They report the whole movement, active and passive parts together. The cancellation fails.
scenes.visual: Row 3 central meter rises to high, its modulation tracking the total motion. Label: total motion.
scenes.narration: They report the whole movement, active and passive parts together. The cancellation fails.

scenes.tts: So in these neurons, cancellation is central, and it holds only while the feedback matches.
scenes.visual: The three-row table complete. Text: central, and conditional on a match.
scenes.narration: So in these neurons, cancellation is central, and it holds only while the feedback matches.

scenes.tts: People show a related pattern. Self-produced touch is rated less ticklish than the same touch from outside.
scenes.visual: Two hands: one touching its own palm, one touched by another person's finger. A tickle meter reads lower for self-touch.
scenes.narration: People show a related pattern. Self-produced touch is rated less ticklish than the same touch from outside.

scenes.tts: In one study, people moved a robot arm with one hand. A second robot touched their other palm.
scenes.visual: Left hand moves a robot arm; a second robot touches the right palm. Caption: Blakemore, Frith and Wolpert, 1999.
scenes.narration: In one study, people moved a robot arm with one hand. A second robot touched their other palm.

scenes.tts: Predict. Add a delay between the movement and the touch. What happens to the tickle?
scenes.visual: A clock icon inserted between the two robots. Tickle meter with a question mark. Text: Predict.
scenes.narration: Predict. Add a delay between the movement and the touch. What happens to the tickle?

scenes.tts: It feels more ticklish with a delay. Rotating the hand's movement against the touch's direction does the same.
scenes.visual: A tickle meter rises as the imposed delay between movement and touch increases. Then the touch path stays straight across the palm while the left-hand movement arrow rotates away from it, and the meter rises again.
scenes.narration: It feels more ticklish with a delay. Rotating the hand's movement against the touch's direction does the same.

scenes.tts: A forward model, predicting a command's sensory result, is one candidate explanation, not a settled one.
scenes.visual: Box: motor command, forward model, predicted touch. Label: one candidate explanation, not settled.
scenes.narration: A forward model, predicting a command's sensory result, is one candidate explanation, not a settled one.

scenes.tts: Mice show a related signal. Some visual cortex neurons respond when the visual flow fails to match running. One reading: a failed prediction.
scenes.visual: A mouse running on a ball; the visual flow stops; a cortical neuron flashes. Caption: Keller and colleagues, 2012. Text: visuomotor mismatch response; consistent with a prediction-error signal.
scenes.narration: Mice show a related signal. Some visual cortex neurons respond when the visual flow fails to match running. One reading: a failed prediction.

scenes.tts: Back to the one idea. Some pathways subtract a prediction of what your own movement causes.
scenes.visual: Title card: some pathways subtract a prediction of what your own movement causes.
scenes.narration: Back to the one idea. Some pathways subtract a prediction of what your own movement causes.

scenes.tts: Take this with you. In these monkey neurons, the subtraction ran only while the feedback matched the prediction.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: in these monkey vestibular neurons, suppression of the active turn required matching proprioceptive feedback. The completed three-row monkey table beneath.
scenes.narration: Take this with you. In these monkey neurons, the subtraction ran only while the feedback matched the prediction.
